Material/process words tend negative; selected discourse words tend positive.
The named vocabularies share one value per familiar word class, not per token.
Material and selected content-word signals weaken for capitals or a final s.
Negative lexical signals strengthen early in a document or after another
negative lexical cue.
Title: headers, chat/tool boundaries and code delimiters have separate rules.
Unrecognized text is near zero. State resets with the document label.
"""

MATERIAL_CLASSES = {

        forward backward back further following later behind ahead'''),
    'evidence/precision': (0.090, 'actually probably exactly rather'),
    'provision/inclusion': (0.059, '''

    'exclusion': (0.055, 'except without never nothing nobody none'),
    'distributive quantifiers': (0.038, 'each every'),

    'first-person plural, nonobject': (0.019, 'we our ours'),
    'plural demonstratives': (0.016, 'these those'),

    'broad quantities': (-0.022, 'all some many much'),
    'uncertainty': (0.026, 'perhaps maybe possibly'),

    'near location': (0.036, 'here'),
    'far location': (-0.030, 'there'),
    'unbounded duration': (-0.040, 'time'),
    'sameness': (-0.040, 'same'),
}


def flatten(classes):
    return {word: value for value, words in classes.values() for word in words.split()}


MATERIAL_VALUES = flatten(MATERIAL_CLASSES)
LANGUAGE_VALUES = flatten(LANGUAGE_CLASSES)
# These lexical classes retain the spelling/case attenuation used for materials.
ATTENUATED_CLASSES = {
    'movement/continuation', 'collection quantifiers', 'quality',
    'production/use', 'far location', 'unbounded duration', 'sameness',
}
ATTENUATED_WORDS = frozenset(
    word for name, (_, words) in LANGUAGE_CLASSES.items()
    if name in ATTENUATED_CLASSES for word in words.split()
)
CHINESE_VALUES = {
    '焊': -0.75,   # welding
    '电池': -0.31, # battery
    '珠': 0.54,    # bead/pearl
    '年': 0.115,   # year
}


def lexical_signal(token):
    word = token.strip()
    if word in CHINESE_VALUES:
        return CHINESE_VALUES[word]
    if not token.startswith(' '):
        return 0.0
    lower = word.lower()
    plural = lower.endswith('s')
    stem = lower[:-1] if plural else lower
    if stem in MATERIAL_VALUES:
        value = MATERIAL_VALUES[stem]
    elif lower in ATTENUATED_WORDS:
        value = LANGUAGE_VALUES[lower]
    else:
        return LANGUAGE_VALUES.get(lower, 0.0)
    if plural:
        value *= 0.70
    if word[:1].isupper():
        value *= 0.70
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc, token = prefix.document_ids[-1], prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        n, previous, previous_signal = 0, '', 0.0
    else:
        _, n, previous, previous_signal = carry
    raw_signal = lexical_signal(token)
    signal = raw_signal
    if signal < 0:
        signal *= (1.20 if n < 10 else 1.0)
        signal *= (1.35 if previous_signal < 0 else 1.0)
    value = -0.0005 + signal
    if n == 0 and token == 'Title':
        value = -0.113
    elif n == 1 and previous == 'Title' and token == ':':
        value = 0.441
    elif token == '<|im_start|>':
        value = -0.219 if n == 0 else -0.022
    elif token == '<|im_end|>':
        value = -0.085 if previous in {'</tool_call>', '</tool_response>'} else 0.060
    elif token == '<tool_response>':
        value = 0.061
    elif token in {'<think>', '</think>'}:
        value = 0.018 if token == '<think>' else -0.024
    elif previous == '<|im_start|>' and token in {'user', 'assistant'}:
        value = -0.025 if n == 1 else 0.017
    elif previous == '<|im_end|>' and token == '\n':
        value = 0.017
    elif token == '```':
        value = -0.071
    elif token == ' `':
        value = 0.073 if previous.strip() == '`' else 0.030
    elif token == '\r':
        value = 0.084
    elif token == ':' and previous.strip().isdigit():
        value = -0.017
    return (doc, n + 1, token, raw_signal), float(value)

"""Predicts layers.0.mlp.down_proj:5824, a rare MLP-output direction in layer 0.

What it does: it fires (about +0.44) on the colon that follows the word "Title" in a
document's header ("Title: ..."), which is the pattern that dominates the component's
strongest harvested windows. Everywhere else it predicts 0.

Why: the component is almost always silent (CI ~ 0), so a near-zero prediction is
the honest default. This version only captures the "Title:" case; it does not
explain the weaker negative responses to some Chinese characters (e.g. 焊, 珠, 电池).
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    is_colon = strings[-1].strip() == ":"
    after_title = len(strings) >= 2 and strings[-2].strip() == "Title"
    value = 0.44 if (is_colon and after_title) else 0.0
    return carry, float(value)

programs.sol:
"""Recognize recurring line-prefix punctuation and indentation.

Comment prefixes (#, //, ///) become much stronger when the same punctuation
has appeared recently or begins the preceding line. Bullets, headings,
quotes and diff signs have smaller boundary-dependent responses. Compiler
directives are kept separate. Words predict zero; whitespace follows a
small rule about line endings and four-column indentation. Escaped line
breaks within a token count as weaker boundaries. Document changes reset
all context.
"""
import math
import re
from collections import deque

READS = ()
DIRECTIVES = {
    'include', 'define', 'undef', 'if', 'ifdef', 'ifndef', 'elif', 'else',
    'endif', 'pragma', 'error', 'warning', 'line', 'import',
}

# Baseline, after line break, after indentation, same previous-line prefix,
# log(1 + recent occurrences), and first non-whitespace token in a document.
MARKERS = {
    '#':   (-0.24, 0.74, 0.63, 1.20, 0.51, 1.48),
    '##':  (0.13, 0.20, 0.44, 1.14, 0.49, 1.37),
    '###': (0.27, 0.10, 0.07, 0.30, 0.20, 0.56),
    '//':  (0.03, 0.81, 0.36, 0.91, 0.41, 1.66),
    '///': (0.74, 1.36, 0.45, 0.29, 0.27, 0.46),
    '/*':  (0.03, 0.21, -0.08, 0.57, 0.16, 0.41),
    '*':   (-0.06, 0.43, 0.39, 0.38, 0.03, 0.13),
    '**':  (-0.07, 0.05, -0.02, 0.34, 0.05, 0.04),
    '-':   (0.00, 0.60, 0.16, 0.08, 0.00, 0.04),
    '--':  (-0.05, 0.49, -0.12, 0.40, 0.02, 0.36),
    '+':   (0.06, 0.78, 0.21, 0.22, -0.01, 0.16),
    '>':   (0.05, 1.11, 0.37, 0.69, 0.02, 0.56),
    '%':   (0.04, 0.90, 0.31, 0.54, 0.04, 0.50),
    '•':   (-0.03, 0.30, 0.03, 0.15, 0.03, 0.12),
    '#[':  (0.50, 0.30, 0.24, 0.07, -0.05, -0.01),
    ';;':  (0.47, 0.70, -0.06, 0.32, 0.13, 0.00),
    'rule': (0.13, 0.10, 0.13, 0.23, 0.15, -0.07),
}


def kind(s):
    x = s.lstrip(' \t').rstrip('\r\n')
    if s and not s.strip(' \t'):
        return 'space' if s == ' ' else 'indent'
    if x.startswith('#'):
        if x.startswith(('#[', '#![')):
            return '#['
        word = re.match(r'#+([a-z]+)', x)
        if word and word[1] in DIRECTIVES:
            return 'directive'
        return '#' * min(3, len(x) - len(x.lstrip('#')))
    if x.startswith(('//', '/*')) and len(x) > 8:
        if not any(c.isalnum() for c in x):
            return 'rule'  # Decorative comment separator.
    for mark in ('///', '//', '/*', '**', '*', '--', '-', '+', '>', '%', ';;'):
        if x.startswith(mark):
            return mark
    if x.startswith(('•', '●', '◦', '▪', '‣')):
        return '•'
    return None


def family(k):
    if k in ('#', '##', '###', '#['):
        return '#'
    if k in ('//', '///', '/*', 'rule'):
        return '//'
    if k in ('*', '**'):
        return '*'
    return '-' if k == '--' else k


def unescape(s):
    return re.sub(r'\\+[nrt]',
                  lambda m: {'n': '\n', 'r': '\r', 't': '\t'}[m[0][-1]], s)


def line_family(line):
    # Numbered source listings have a line number before the actual prefix.
    line = re.sub(r'^\s*\d+\t', '', line).lstrip(' \t\r')
    return family(kind(line))


def whitespace(s, prev, line, oldline):
    newline = prev.endswith('\n')
    tail = prev.rstrip('\r\n \t')
    period = newline and tail.endswith('.')
    code_end = newline and tail.endswith((';', '{', '}', ')'))
    previous_space = bool(prev) and not prev.strip(' \t')
    escaped = prev.endswith('\\n')
    blank = prev.count('\n') > 1
    if s == ' ':
        return (-0.005 - 0.13*newline + 0.11*period - 0.09*code_end
                - 0.03*previous_space - 0.05*escaped - 0.11*blank)
    # Such tokens often omit the leading space belonging to the next token.
    four_column_indent = (not line.strip() and not s.strip(' ')
                          and len(s) % 4 == 3)
    return (-0.07 + 0.26*newline + 0.18*period - 0.17*code_end
            + 0.10*previous_space + 0.14*escaped - 0.10*(s == '\t')
            - 0.12*four_column_indent + 0.16*min(len(oldline), 100)/100
            - 0.06*blank)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = int(prefix.document_ids[-1])
    if carry is None or carry['doc'] != doc:
        carry = dict(doc=doc, line='', oldline='', oldkind=None, prev='',
                     first=True, recent=deque(maxlen=128))
    c = carry
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    clean = unescape(s) if '\\' in s else s
    k = kind(s)
    fam = family(k)
    value = 0.0
    if k in ('space', 'indent'):
        value = whitespace(s, c['prev'], c['line'], c['oldline'])
    elif k == 'directive':
        value = 0.1
    elif k in MARKERS:
        previous = unescape(c['prev'])
        at_margin = not c['line'].strip()
        numbered = bool(re.fullmatch(r'\s*\d+\t[ \t]*', c['line']))
        same_prefix = (at_margin or numbered) and c['oldkind'] == fam
        boundary = previous.endswith('\n') * (
            1.0 if c['prev'].endswith('\n') else 0.45)
        indentation = bool(previous) and not previous.strip(' \t\r')
        count = sum(old == fam for old in c['recent'])
        b, br, ind, repeat, recur, first = MARKERS[k]
        value = (b + br*boundary + ind*indentation + repeat*same_prefix
                 + recur*math.log1p(count) + first*c['first'])
        if '\n' in s:
            value *= 0.55
        value = min(4.5, max(0.0, value))

    if '\n' in clean:
        parts = (c['line'] + clean).split('\n')
        c['oldline'], c['line'] = parts[-2], parts[-1][:250]
        c['oldkind'] = line_family(c['oldline'])
    else:
        c['line'] = (c['line'] + clean)[:250]
    if clean.strip():
        c['first'] = False
    c['prev'] = s
    c['recent'].append(fam)
    return c, float(value)

"""Layer-0 MLP down_proj, component 5826: a "start of a comment or list item" detector.

It fires on the marker token that opens a line of code or prose: a comment opener
(#, ##, //, ///, /*) or a bullet (-, +, *, >, •). It fires hardest on a comment opener
that continues a run of comment lines (the previous non-blank line also opened with a
comment marker). A comment opener after code on the same line fires weakly. Everything
else, including the indentation before the marker, is predicted as 0.
"""

READS = ()

COMMENT = {"#", "##", "###", "####", "//", "///", "/*"}
BULLET = {"-", "--", "+", "*", ">", "•"}

# Typical activation (in the model's units) for each situation.
COMMENT_CONTINUING = 2.2  # comment opener on a line, previous non-blank line was a comment
COMMENT_NEW_BLOCK = 0.8  # comment opener on a line after code or after a blank line
BULLET_OPENER = 0.7  # list / bullet marker opening a line
COMMENT_AFTER_CODE = 0.6  # comment opener later on a line, after code


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry = (seen, prev_comment): seen = a visible token has already appeared on this line;
    # prev_comment = the last non-blank line opened with a comment marker.
    seen, prev_comment = (False, False) if carry is None else carry
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    s = tok.strip()
    value = 0.0
    if s != "" and not seen:
        # first visible token of its line: is it a line-opening marker?
        if s in COMMENT:
            value = COMMENT_CONTINUING if prev_comment else COMMENT_NEW_BLOCK
        elif s in BULLET:
            value = BULLET_OPENER
        prev_comment = s in COMMENT
        seen = True
    elif s in COMMENT:
        value = COMMENT_AFTER_CODE
    if "\n" in tok:
        seen = False
    return (seen, prev_comment), value

"""Lexical detector for layer-0 MLP down_proj component 5827.

What it does: it reads only the newest token and predicts a positive activation when that
token is one of a few kinds of word that this component responds to. Everything else

Only whitespace tokens containing a newline receive a nonzero prediction.

makes long lines fire more strongly. The document's first line break has a
larger response. Punctuation-only preceding tokens and sentence endings
weaken it. Formatting, the number of earlier line breaks, and a closing
reasoning tag provide small adjustments. State resets between documents.

        if breaks == 0:
            value = 0.085 + 0.889 * math.tanh(size / 230.0)
        else:
            value = 0.024 + 0.745 * math.tanh(
                max(size - 66.8, 0) / 285.0)
        previous = previous.strip()
        if previous and not any(c.isalnum() for c in previous):
            value *= 0.453
        value += 0.056 * (min(token.count('\n'), 3) - 1)
        value -= 0.024 * math.log1p(breaks)
        value += 0.049 * previous.isalpha()
        value -= 0.084 * (last_character in SENTENCE_ENDS)
        value -= 0.059 * ('\r' in token)
        value += 0.0058 * min(token.count(' '), 10)
        value += 0.037 * ('\t' in token)
        value += 0.119 * (previous == '</think>')

        breaks += token.count('\n')

        last_character = suffix.rstrip()[-1:] or ''

        length += len(token)
        line_tokens += 1
        last_character = token.rstrip()[-1:] or last_character

    return state, float(value)

Examples are '_b' + 'ash', '/S' + 'ymbol', and '\\tr' + 'ule'.
The response is negative, with strengths set by onset length, case,
and the separator. Short onsets usually respond most strongly.
Ordinary space-prefixed words have little response. Backslash escapes
and continuations after accented letters or digits are excluded;
unlikely English consonant onsets are weakened.

not a vocabulary lookup; individual words can differ substantially.
Small baselines cover row/document starts and bare capital initials.
The carry keeps only the preceding token and resets at document changes.

import re

# Common consonant clusters that can begin an English syllable.
ONSETS = set('''bl br ch cl cr dr fl fr gl gr kn ph pl pr qu sc sh sk
                sl sm sn sp st sw th tr tw wh wr scr shr spl spr str thr'''.split())
LETTERS_AT_END = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z]+$')
# Single-letter onsets: lowercase strength, capitalized strength.
STRENGTH = {
    'bracket': (0.95, 1.55),
    'dot': (0.65, 1.25),
    'slash': (0.90, 1.50),
    'hyphen': (0.70, 0.82),
    'underscore': (0.60, 1.20),
    'tab': (1.05, 1.65),
    'comma': (1.35, 0.95),
    'other': (0.45, 1.05),
}


def separator(boundary):
    if boundary[-1].isalnum():
        return None  # This is still inside a word, not a punctuation boundary.
    if '\\' in boundary:
        return None  # Serialized escapes are not word onsets.
    if '\t' in boundary:
        return 'tab'
    for sign, kind in ((',', 'comma'), ('/', 'slash'), ('.', 'dot'),
                       ('-', 'hyphen'), ('_', 'underscore')):
        if sign in boundary:
            return kind
    if any(c in boundary for c in '([{'):
        return 'bracket'
    return 'other'


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    state = (doc, token)
    if not (token.isascii() and token.isalpha()):
        return state, 0.0
    if not previous:
        return state, GAIN * 0.07
    if not (token.islower() or token.isupper()):
        return state, 0.0
    match = LETTERS_AT_END.search(previous)
    if match is None:
        return state, 0.0
    onset = match[0]
    boundary = previous[:match.start()]
    n = len(onset)
    if not boundary or not boundary.strip(' '):
        # Bare capital initials also sometimes mark an incomplete word.
        value = -0.12 if not boundary and n == 1 and onset.isupper() else 0.0
        return state, GAIN * value
    kind = separator(boundary)
    if kind is None:
        return state, 0.0
    lower, capital = STRENGTH[kind]
    if onset.istitle():
        strength = capital
        if n > 2:
            strength *= 0.5
        if token.isupper():
            strength *= 0.8 if len(token) == 1 else 0.5

        strength = lower / n ** (1.5 if kind in ('dot', 'slash') else 0.5)
        if token.isupper():
            strength = 0.15

    joined = (onset + token).lower()
    consonants = re.match(r'[^aeiouy]*', joined)[0]
    plausible = len(consonants) <= 1 or consonants in ONSETS
    if not plausible and len(token) > 1:
        strength = min(strength, 0.4) if onset.istitle() else 0.04
    return state, -GAIN * strength
